data.title: Invest In Infra, Registrations And Test Facilities Before Expecting Any Order: SRL's CMD
data.description:
Shree Refrigerations’ R.G. Shende says mission-critical indigenisation demands years of demonstrated performance on board naval vessels, steady servicing and a willingness to build Navy feedback into product upgrades

India’s defence indigenisation push has moved from policy to practice, but the real test lies in the small and mid-sized firms that supply the “invisible” subsystems inside large platforms. R.G. Shende, Chairman and Managing Director of Shree Refrigerations Limited (SRL), says his company developed air conditioning for Scorpene submarines without foreign collaboration. In this interview, he explains what it takes to earn the Indian Navy’s trust, why infrastructure and test facilities must come before orders, and why policy should reserve MSME benefits for companies with at least 51 per cent local ownership.

India has set ambitious goals for defence indigenisation and exports, backed by positive indigenous lists and rising capital budgets. How far has the country come in building real domestic capability, as opposed to assembling imported systems, and where is the gap still widest?

For a country that builds rockets and all the high-tech equipment, defence indigenisation comes naturally and without much technological challenge. All it needed was governmental buying and support for indigenisation by way of negative lists and mandatory local content. Although some equipment needs to be imported due to economic considerations, most manufacturing and integration can be local, cutting dependence on foreign tech.

The government also supports tech development through the indigenisation push in schemes such as iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence) and ADITI (Acing Development of Innovative Technologies with iDEX). Tech support is also available from DRDO by way of Transfer of Technology (ToT) to private enterprises. Patient capital is also made available for innovation funding. The results are there to be seen. In our own case, we were able to develop ACs for Scorpene submarines without any foreign collaboration.

Large defence platforms are built on the work of hundreds of specialised suppliers, many of them small and mid-sized, in areas such as cooling, controls and fabrication. Why do these “invisible” subsystems matter so much to a platform’s performance, and are they getting the attention and support they deserve?

Definitely. Dependence on foreign vendors needs to be reduced to a minimum to avoid a big drain on forex outflow. Quality control by the Director General of Quality Control (DGQA) ensures that the equipment is up to the exacting standards of workmanship and quality. All this happens at a fraction of the cost of imported equipment and service. Besides, post-installation service is also available locally and is highly price competitive.

Replacing an imported subsystem with an Indian-made one demands engineering depth, testing and years of trust-building with the Indian Navy. What does it actually take to indigenise a mission-critical system, and what do people outside the industry underestimate?

Perseverance, patience and focus are needed to demonstrate a firm’s commitment to serving the Navy. The firm has to establish credentials that take years to build and moments to lose. That is where the promoter’s (and his team’s) integrity and firm commitment matter. This is not for the faint-hearted. The ability to develop tech, demonstrate it on board naval vessels over a longer duration, service it over the years, and integrate Naval feedback into product upgrades are the important aspects.

Naval platforms need cooling and climate control that works in extreme heat, humidity, vibration and confined spaces, while energy efficiency and reliability are rising priorities. Which technologies will shape the next generation of marine and defence HVAC, and how ready is India to build them at home?

The focus here is more on stealth, reliability and serviceability. All the tech is available within India. Firms only have to rise to the occasion, bring out their best and deliver.

You spent over two decades in commercial refrigeration and air conditioning before turning towards defence. What did you have to unlearn, build or invest in to make that shift, and what advice would you give mid-sized industrial companies considering the same path?

Have heart, believe in yourself, ensure deep pockets and go for it. More importantly, invest in infra, registrations and a test facility before expecting any order. These are prerequisites and not something to be done “after I get the order”. The advantage here is long-term visibility of business, which allows you to build capacity and capability ahead of the market opportunity.

Defence manufacturing involves long approval cycles, rigorous qualification and large working-capital needs, and public markets are now showing strong interest in the sector. How should mid-sized defence suppliers balance patient, long-gestation growth with the expectations of investors?

Efficiency. That’s it. Invest in modernisation, better project execution capability, lower cash cycles and a strong order book. If the forces have faith in you, investors will.

India’s defence ecosystem is opening up to private players of all sizes, yet procurement processes remain demanding and slow for newcomers. What reforms would do the most to bring more capable private manufacturers into the supply chain and keep them there?

The government has done enough. It is time for Indian industry to rise to the occasion and demonstrate its skills and commitment. There is some scope for improvement in expediting payments, especially to MSMEs; this, over and above the TReDS channel, will help. The anomaly is that large foreign OEMs open a small office in India, harvest the local supply chains, become MSMEs in India and enjoy all the benefits of a local MSME. These firms have access to large overseas funds and can easily leverage their foreign clout to outbid a local MSME. The challenge is that the equipment still has foreign IP. This is not in line with Aatmanirbhar Bharat, although it may qualify under the Make in India norms of x per cent local content. This defeats the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. Policymakers need to review the policy to ensure that the benefits are available to companies with a minimum of 51 per cent local ownership. This will ensure higher participation of Indian MSMEs in this national capability-building initiative.

Looking ahead 10 years, what would a self-reliant Indian defence supply chain look like, in terms of exports, technology ownership and the role of small and mid-sized companies, and what has to happen to get there?

Companies requiring after-sales service support will find it challenging to export to foreign nations. The business volume needs to justify creating a service infrastructure in the customer country. Also, most countries would like to emulate their own version of “Make in My Country”. Exports are possible by way of JVs with local companies. Again, companies need to create that level of credibility. They also need to exhibit at foreign expos and trade shows, and demonstrate their capability, reference list, infrastructure and service capability at short notice. Again, build credibility and trust. This is a long process and there are no shortcuts.

Savi Khanna

BW Reporters Assistant Editor, BW Businessworld

data.title: Lemon Tree Hotels signs Keys Lite property in Bhilwara
data.description:
Lemon Tree Hotels Limited has signed Keys Lite by Lemon Tree Hotels, Bhilwara, strengthening its presence in Rajasthan. The property will be managed by Carnation Hotels Private Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Lemon Tree Hotels Limited.

Located in Bhilwara, a commercial centre known for its textile industry and business activity, the hotel will cater to business and leisure travellers. The property will feature 63 rooms, a restaurant, banquet facilities, a meeting/conference room, a fitness centre and other public areas.

Vishvapreet Singh Cheema, president, Lemon Tree Hotels Limited, said, "Rajasthan continues to be an important growth market for us, defined by a strong mix of commercial dynamism and rich tourism. Bhilwara, a key textile and industrial centre, presents a natural opportunity for Keys Lite to cater to the rising demand for reliable, value-driven hospitality. This signing scales our footprint to 24 hotels in the state and underscores our focused approach to expanding across India’s key industrial hubs and emerging secondary markets."

Bhilwara Railway Station is approximately 1.5 km from the property, while Maharana Pratap Airport in Udaipur is approximately 148 km away. With this signing, Lemon Tree Hotels will have 14 operational and 10 upcoming hotels in Rajasthan.

data.title: BPCL Q2 Profit Falls 21% To Rs 4,863 Cr As Margins Weigh
data.description:
Higher revenue from operations was offset by lower marketing margins on certain petroleum products, while first-half profit fell sharply

Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) reported a 21.4 per cent year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 4,863.05 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 6,191.49 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Revenue from operations rose 29.8 per cent to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore a year earlier. Total expenses increased to Rs 1.52 lakh crore from Rs 1.15 lakh crore, while profit before tax, including the share of profit from equity-accounted investees and exceptional items, declined to Rs 6,559.80 crore from Rs 8,344.59 crore.

The company’s standalone results showed a similar trend, with net profit falling 22.5 per cent year on year to Rs 4,993.17 crore from Rs 6,442.53 crore. Standalone revenue from operations increased to Rs 1.58 lakh crore from Rs 1.22 lakh crore.

For the first half of FY27, BPCL’s consolidated net profit declined to Rs 2,990.35 crore from Rs 13,030.51 crore in the corresponding period last year. Consolidated revenue from operations rose to Rs 3.17 lakh crore from Rs 2.51 lakh crore.

Marketing Margins Weigh

BPCL said lower profit during April-September 2026 was mainly due to suppressed marketing margins on certain petroleum products, partly offset by higher refining margins.

The company also reported a cumulative net negative buffer of Rs 17,334.40 crore in its liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) account as of 30 September 2026, up from Rs 12,318.52 crore at the end of March. Revenue from LPG sales has not been recognised to the extent of this negative buffer.

The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas had approved compensation of Rs 7,594 crore towards under-recoveries on domestic LPG sales incurred up to March 2025 and expected up to March 2026. BPCL recognised six monthly installments aggregating Rs 3,796.98 crore during the first half of FY27.

BPCL’s refinery throughput increased to 10.41 million tonne in the September quarter from 9.82 million tonne a year earlier. Domestic market sales rose to 13.47 million tonne from 12.67 million tonne, while export sales increased to 0.59 million tonne from 0.36 million tonne.

data.title: Lava International Faces Leadership Shake-Up Amid Rs 600 Cr Fundraise Plans
data.description:
The handset maker is targeting the sub-Rs 20,000 smartphone segment while reportedly exploring a Rs 500–600 crore fundraise

Lava International Managing Director Sunil Raina and Chief Financial Officer Rajesh Sethi are set to step down from their respective roles by December, as the Indian smartphone maker looks to secure fresh capital and revive business growth. Co-founder Hari Om Rai, who stepped down as managing director in 2023, has returned to the role.

A company spokesperson confirmed the departures, saying that Raina and Sethi had decided to move on from their positions. Sethi was acknowledged for his contributions to the company’s financial operations and business priorities.

Leadership Changes At Lava

According to reports, both executives have submitted their resignations and are serving their notice periods, with their exits expected by December. Raina is reportedly leaving to pursue business ventures outside Lava.Raina joined Lava in 2010 as Vice-President and Chief Marketing Officer before moving through several senior positions. He took over as interim managing director in November 2023 after Rai was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate in a money-laundering case linked to Vivo. Raina was formally elevated to managing director in June 2025.

Sethi joined Lava as Group Chief Financial Officer in May 2024. Before joining the handset maker, he worked with Iraq-based Ster Group and held positions at Bharti Airtel, Telenor Group and Essar Group.The latest departures follow the exit of Sanjeev Agarwal, who served as Chief Manufacturing Officer and later as Executive Director and Chief Manufacturing Officer at Lava.

Focus On Affordable Smartphones

The leadership changes come as Lava seeks to strengthen its position in the smartphone segment priced below Rs 20,000. The company has previously said its smartphone business grew by 60–70 per cent during the year, despite a contraction in the overall market.The sub-Rs 20,000 segment represents an opportunity for the company as it seeks to revive growth and expand its market presence.

Fundraising And Stake Sale Talks

Lava is also reportedly exploring a fundraise of around Rs 500–600 crore to finance expansion and potentially restructure part of its debt.Earlier reports have suggested that promoters of electronics manufacturers Dixon Technologies and Amber Enterprises are in discussions to acquire stakes in Lava in their personal capacities. The reported discussions and fundraising plans come as the company navigates leadership changes and seeks fresh capital to support its next phase of growth.

data.title: Tech Mahindra Acquires Finastra’s Cash Management Suite
data.description:
The deal adds cash management, virtual accounts and liquidity management products to Tech Mahindra’s banking technology portfolio

Tech Mahindra has acquired the cash management product suite of Finastra, comprising Fusion Cash Management, Fusion Virtual Accounts and Fusion Liquidity Management, expanding its portfolio of banking technology solutions. The financial details of the transaction have not been disclosed.

The acquisition is aimed at supporting continued product investment, innovation and business growth within Tech Mahindra’s Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) business. It also provides for continuity of services and support for existing customers while bringing product engineering and customer success professionals into Tech Mahindra.

Expanding Banking Solutions

The acquired portfolio includes three products covering cash management, virtual accounts and liquidity management. These solutions form part of the technology infrastructure used by financial institutions to manage corporate banking and treasury-related requirements.

The addition broadens Tech Mahindra’s banking solutions portfolio as it continues to develop its offerings for the financial services sector.

Focus On Product Development

Tech Mahindra intends to continue investing in the acquired products, with a focus on innovation and growth within its BFSI business. The transaction also brings experienced product engineering talent into the company, supporting the ongoing development and management of the suite.

Customer success professionals are also part of the talent transition, helping maintain support for organisations already using the products.

Customer Service Continuity

The acquisition includes provisions for continued services and support for existing customers. This is intended to maintain operational continuity as the products and associated teams transition to Tech Mahindra.

The financial terms of the deal and further details about the integration process have not been disclosed.

The transaction adds to Tech Mahindra’s banking technology capabilities through an established suite of cash and liquidity management products, while placing continued product investment and customer support among the stated priorities of the acquisition.

data.title: STL Appoints Lakshmi Iyer To Lead M&A & Capital Market Strategy
data.description:
The corporate development executive joins from Tata Power, where she worked on strategic capital allocation exceeding USD 3 billion

Sterlite Technologies (STL) has appointed Lakshmi Iyer as Chief – Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A), Investor Relations and Capital Markets Strategy, effective October 2026. Iyer joins the optical connectivity solutions provider after nearly three years at Tata Power, where she served as Head – Strategic Finance and M&A, working on capital allocation across energy-transition initiatives.

In her new role, Iyer will focus on mergers and acquisitions, strategic partnerships, investor relations and capital markets strategy as STL looks to pursue growth opportunities in optical connectivity. The appointment comes amid rising demand for connectivity infrastructure, driven in part by the expansion of artificial intelligence-led data centres.

Experience Across Capital Allocation

At Tata Power, Iyer worked on strategic capital allocation exceeding USD 3 billion across energy-transition initiatives. Her responsibilities included supporting investments intended to contribute to the energy sector’s transition.

She held the position of Head – Strategic Finance and M&A from January 2024 to September 2026. Before joining Tata Power, she had also worked at STL from May 2021 to December 2023 as Head – Mergers and Acquisitions and Investor Relations.

Extensive Deal Experience

Iyer brings around 25 years of experience in corporate development and investments, with a focus on cross-border M&A, capital raising and take-private transactions. Her experience spans energy, core infrastructure, industrials and technology across Asia-Pacific, Africa, North America, Europe and the Middle East.

She previously spent more than four years at GMR Group as Head – Mergers, Divestments and Acquisitions, followed by over eight years at Essar in a senior M&A and capital-raising role.

Her work has included buy-side and sell-side transactions, debt and equity fundraising, and complex deals involving multiple markets and regulatory frameworks. Her cumulative deal experience exceeds USD 15 billion, according to her professional profile.

Focus On Optical Connectivity

At STL, Iyer will work across M&A, investor relations and capital markets strategy. The company operates in optical connectivity, a segment facing increasing infrastructure requirements as AI-led data centres expand.

Her return to STL follows her earlier tenure at the company in an M&A and investor relations leadership role. The combination of her previous experience at STL and her more recent work in energy-sector investments at Tata Power brings together exposure to technology infrastructure, strategic finance and capital allocation.

Iyer holds a Master of Business Administration from SDA Bocconi and has completed an executive programme in general management and leadership at Columbia Business School.

data.title: KEC International Bags Rs 2,872 Cr Power Grid Orders For kV765 Lines
data.description:
The contracts will support the evacuation of 8.5 GW of renewable energy from Gujarat, taking KEC International’s FY27 year-to-date order intake beyond Rs 13,500 crore

KEC International has secured orders worth Rs 2,872 crore from Power Grid Corporation of India (PGCIL) for the design, supply and installation of 765 kV transmission lines. The projects will facilitate the evacuation of 8.5 gigawatts (GW) of renewable energy from Gujarat, according to a regulatory filing dated 24 October.

The company said the contracts represent the largest-ever single order for its India transmission and distribution (T&D) business, significantly expanding its domestic order book.

Vimal Kejriwal, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of KEC International, said the latest contracts reflected continued momentum in the company's T&D business. "These prestigious 765 kV projects, associated with the evacuation of 8.5 GW of renewable energy from Gujarat, have substantially expanded our India T&D order book," Kejriwal said.

The company remains confident about the growth prospects of India's T&D sector, supported by rising energy demand and the country's continued focus on strengthening transmission infrastructure. With the latest wins, KEC International's cumulative order intake for the current financial year to date has crossed Rs 13,500 crore. The T&D business accounts for around Rs 9,500 crore of this total, the company said.

Headquartered in Mumbai, KEC International is the flagship infrastructure engineering, procurement and construction company of RPG Group. Its business portfolio includes power transmission and distribution, civil construction, transportation, renewable energy, oil and gas pipelines, and cables and conductors.

KEC International shares closed around 1.5 per cent lower at Rs 327 apiece on the National Stock Exchange on 23 October. The stock has declined nearly 56 per cent so far in 2026.

data.title: India's emerging sectors to drive capex, credit demand towards storage, semiconductors: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Financing demand in India's emerging sectors is expected to shift towards battery storage, semiconductor packaging, green hydrogen projects with assured buyers and defence suppliers over the next three to five years, as investments in new growth industries create opportunities for banks, according to a Union Bank of India research report.

The report noted artificial intelligence (AI), semiconductors and defence is likely to lead the investment pipeline, with indicative public and private investments of around Rs 5.9 lakh crore, Rs 5.27 lakh crore and Rs 5.07 lakh crore, respectively.

It said financing opportunities would increasingly emerge in advanced packaging and assembly of semiconductors, battery recycling, lithium iron phosphate (LFP) and sodium-ion battery capacity, storage infrastructure and component suppliers to the defence industry.

The report also highlighted the potential for financing hydrogen projects backed by assured offtake agreements, while demand for data centres is expected to expand towards edge and colocation facilities as AI inference grows.

However, the report cautioned that technology obsolescence, uncertain revenues, delayed payments and long investment payback periods remain significant risks for lenders.

Semiconductor projects typically have payback periods of five to eight years, while space projects may take seven to ten years, exceeding conventional loan tenures, it said. AI infrastructure also faces rapid technology cycles, with graphics processing unit clusters requiring upgrades every 18 to 24 months.

The report said ten of the twelve emerging sectors already had identifiable debt-financing routes, while AI and space remained predominantly equity-funded due to technology risks and long payback periods.

It recommended that banks develop specialised lending capabilities for semiconductors, hydrogen, data centres and battery storage, alongside products such as milestone-linked disbursements, receivables financing, equipment leasing and green loans.

The report identified renewable energy, semiconductors, green hydrogen and critical minerals as sectors suited to project finance and development finance institution-led funding, while electric vehicles and drones could benefit from asset financing and non-banking financial company lending.

India's renewable energy capacity stood at 288.6 GW against a target of 500 GW by 2030, while the electric vehicle and battery storage market was projected to grow from USD 34 billion to USD 113 billion by 2030.

The report said financing opportunities would increasingly move towards commercially viable projects and supply-chain participants as these emerging sectors expand.

data.title: Compass Therapeutics, Inc. (CMPX) Posts Positive Phase 2/3 BTC Results
data.description:
Key points:
  • As published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (JCO) and presented at ESMO, COMPANION-002 met its primary endpoint of ORR and key secondary endpoint of PFS, with a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.
  • Responses were durable, with a median duration of response (DOR) of 4.9 months, and disease control rate (DCR) was also significantly improved (62.2% vs. 36.8%).
  • A new, post hoc analysis of overall survival (OS) included in the JCO publication uses the Two-Stage Estimation, an established method for adjusting for crossover, and demonstrates an OS hazard ratio of 0.85 (95% CI, 0.59–1.26; p=0.53).

Compass Therapeutics published Phase 2/3 data showing tovecimig plus paclitaxel improved ORR to 18.0% vs 5.3% and median PFS to 4.7 vs 2.6 months (HR=0.44) in previously treated advanced biliary tract cancer.

data.title: Johnson & Johnson's prostate cancer drug shrinks tumors in early-stage trial
data.description:
Johnson & Johnson on Saturday said its experimental once-daily oral prostate cancer drug caused tumors to disappear or shrink in an early-stage trial.

J&J had gained access to the drug through its $3.05 billion deal to buy Halda Therapeutics last year.

Here are more details:

  • The company was testing JNJ-6143 in patients with advanced prostate cancer who had received multiple treatments

  • Its novel approach selectively kills cancer cells by interfering with a protein they need to survive

  • In the trial, 77% of 31 evaluable patients receiving the 50-milligram dose saw their PSA levels, a blood marker used to monitor prostate cancer, fall by at least 50%; in 48% of patients, PSA levels fell by at least 90%

  • Among patients whose tumors could be measured using imaging, 69% had a confirmed complete or partial response

  • "It adds a new mechanism of action to J&J's prostate cancer portfolio," a Johnson & Johnson spokesperson said

  • Common side effects were nausea and elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels. One patient discontinued treatment due to adverse effects

  • The data were presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress

  • A new, post hoc analysis of overall survival (OS) included in the JCO publication uses the Two-Stage Estimation, an established method for adjusting for crossover, and demonstrates an OS hazard ratio of 0.85 (95% CI, 0.59–1.26; p=0.53).
  • Safety profile was consistent with prior tovecimig studies and the anti-VEGF class, with no new safety signals identified.

BOSTON, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Compass Therapeutics, Inc. , a clinical-stage, oncology-focused biopharmaceutical company developing proprietary antibody-based therapeutics to treat multiple human diseases, today announced the publication of results from the positive Phase 2/3 COMPANION-002 study of tovecimig in combination with paclitaxel in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC) in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (JCO). The results are also being presented today by Nilofer S. Azad, M.D., Johns Hopkins Sidney Kimmel Comprehensive Cancer Center, at the 2026 European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in Madrid, Spain. The full publication is available via open access at https://ascopubs.org/toc/jco/0/ja.

COMPANION-002 is a randomized Phase 2/3 study that evaluated tovecimig plus paclitaxel versus paclitaxel alone in 168 patients with advanced BTC who had received one prior therapy. As previously reported, and now published following peer review, the study met its primary endpoint, with tovecimig plus paclitaxel demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in ORR of 18.0% vs. 5.3% with paclitaxel alone (p=0.0228) evaluated by blinded independent central review (BICR). The study also met its key secondary endpoint of PFS with a median PFS of 4.7 vs. 2.6 months (HR=0.44, p<0.0001), representing a 56% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death.

Key findings from COMPANION-002 include:

  • Duration of response and disease control: Responses with tovecimig plus paclitaxel lasted a median of 4.9 months. The disease control rate, which includes patients whose cancer responded or remained stable, significantly improved at 62.2% vs. 36.8% with paclitaxel alone (p=0.0018).
  • Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma subgroup: Patients with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (cancer of the bile ducts inside the liver), a prespecified subgroup, made up more than half of the study population (92 of 168). In these patients, results were consistent with the overall study population, with an ORR of 15.3% vs. 0% (p=0.0258) and median PFS of 5.1 vs. 3.0 months (HR=0.32).
  • Overall survival (OS) and crossover-adjusted analysis: Patients in the paclitaxel arm could cross over to tovecimig plus paclitaxel arm after BICR-confirmed progression. 31 of 57 (54%) patients crossed over, resulting in 85% of all patients in the study (142 of 168) ultimately receiving tovecimig. The intent-to-treat OS analysis was confounded by the high rate of crossover and no statistically significant difference in OS was observed. To estimate the treatment effect if crossover had not occurred, the JCO publication includes a post hoc exploratory analysis using the Two-Stage Estimation, an established method for adjusting for crossover, in which the OS hazard ratio was 0.85 (95% CI, 0.59–1.26; p=0.53).
  • Outcomes in crossover patients: Among the 31 patients who crossed over, median PFS after the addition of tovecimig to paclitaxel, a prespecified secondary endpoint, was 3.5 months, compared with 1.9 months during their initial treatment with paclitaxel alone (HR=0.40, p=0.0035). In a post hoc exploratory analysis, these patients who crossed over to receive tovecimig had a median OS of 12.8 months, compared with 6.1 months for control-arm patients who did not cross over (HR=0.54, p=0.04), even though crossover patients had progressed more quickly on initial paclitaxel treatment. These crossover comparisons were not randomized and are exploratory.
  • Safety: The safety profile was generally manageable and consistent with prior tovecimig studies and the anti-VEGF class, with no new safety signals identified. The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) in the combination arm were hypertension (69%) and fatigue (67%). Grade 3 or higher TEAEs occurred in 93.5% of patients in the combination arm and 64.2% of patients who received paclitaxel alone. TEAEs leading to overall treatment discontinuation occurred in 27.8% and 11.3%, respectively, and were mostly consistent with known anti-angiogenic and chemotherapy toxicities. No hypertensive crises or unexpected severe cardiovascular toxicities were observed. TEAEs leading to death occurred in 5.6% and 1.9% of patients, respectively.

“COMPANION-002 is an important, randomized study in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer,” said Dr. Azad. “The significant improvements in response rate and progression-free survival, together with the durability of responses and disease control, are encouraging for patients in this setting. We also saw activity in patients who switched to tovecimig after their disease progressed on paclitaxel alone, which is notable in a setting where disease often progresses quickly.”

"Publication of the COMPANION-002 results in the Journal of Clinical Oncology following independent peer review is a significant milestone for patients with BTC," said Thomas Schuetz, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Compass. "These data, including the new two-stage estimation adjusting for the crossover impact on overall survival, strengthen our conviction that tovecimig has the potential to make a meaningful difference for patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer who have few treatment options. We are determined to bring tovecimig to these patients and will continue working with the FDA toward that goal."

Additional analyses from COMPANION-002, including patient-reported quality of life and translational research, are ongoing and will be reported separately.

About Tovecimig

Tovecimig is an investigational DLL4 x VEGF-A bispecific antibody designed to block two angiogenic pathways simultaneously, representing a first-in-class approach to disrupting tumor angiogenesis. In COMPANION-002, tovecimig was evaluated in combination with paclitaxel in patients with previously treated, advanced biliary tract cancer. Tovecimig has received Fast Track and Orphan Drug Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Tovecimig remains investigational and has not been approved by the FDA.

About Biliary Tract Cancer

BTC is an aggressive, life-threatening cancer estimated to affect approximately 26,500 patients annually in the United States. For the vast majority of patients with BTC whose tumors do not harbor an actionable mutation with an approved targeted therapy, there is currently no FDA-approved treatment in the second-line setting. The therapies most commonly used in this setting, which are not labeled or approved by the FDA for the treatment of patients with BTC, generally have an ORR of approximately 5% or less.

About COMPANION-002

COMPANION-002 (NCT05506943) is a randomized, controlled Phase 2/3 study of tovecimig in patients with unresectable advanced, metastatic or recurrent BTC who received one prior systemic chemotherapy regimen. The study randomized 168 patients 2:1 to tovecimig plus paclitaxel (n=111) or paclitaxel alone (n=57). The primary endpoint was ORR by blinded independent central review; secondary endpoints included PFS, OS and duration of response.

The company leverages deep expertise in tumor biology and proprietary antibody engineering technologies to develop differentiated therapies that target the intersection of angiogenesis, immune activation, and tumor-driven immunosuppression. data.description:
Median PFS was 21.5 months with the gedatolisib triplet and 11.5 months with the gedatolisib doublet versus 9.1 months with alpelisib + fulvestrant in patients who had no liver metastases

ORR and median duration of response was 59% and 19.4 months for the gedatolisib triplet and 43% and 27.8 months for the gedatolisib doublet, respectively, compared to 33% and 7.5 months for alpelisib + fulvestrant

The discontinuation rate for gedatolisib due to treatment-emergent adverse events was 5% and 4% with the gedatolisib triplet and doublet, respectively, compared to 19% for alpelisib

MINNEAPOLIS, Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Celcuity Inc. , a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing targeted therapies for the treatment of multiple solid tumor indications, today announced new subgroup analyses from the PIK3CA mutant (“MT”) cohort of the Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 study evaluating gedatolisib in patients with HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (“ABC”). These data were presented by Dr. Barbara Pistilli, Head of the Breast Cancer Unit, Gustave Roussy, at the European Society of Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 today, Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 4:15 a.m. EST/10:15 a.m. CEST during a late breaking rapid oral presentation:

Grade 3 stomatitis with gedatolisib was transient. By the second cycle of treatment, less than 3% of patients had Grade 3 stomatitis, and all grade 3 events improved within 1-2 weeks. Discontinuations due to stomatitis for the gedatolisib triplet and gedatolisib doublet were minimal, 1% and 0%, respectively.

“The additional data from Study 2 of VIKTORIA-1 show consistent and significant clinical benefit for important sub-groups of breast cancer patients treated with gedatolisib regimens,” said Igor Gorbachevsky, Chief Medical Officer of Celcuity. “For patients who do not have liver metastases and received the gedatolisib triplet, the median progression-free survival was approximately 21 months, versus approximately 9 months for the alpelisib regimen. This is a particularly important result since patients with no liver metastases represent approximately 60%-70% of all patients treated in this setting.”

“Additionally, the median duration of response was over 19 months for the gedatolisib triplet in both the PIK3CA wild-type cohort, or Study 1, and the PIK3CA mutant cohort, or Study 2, compared to not evaluable for fulvestrant in the PIK3CA wild-type cohort and 7.5 months for alpelisib plus fulvestrant in the PIK3CA mutant cohort. To our knowledge, the gedatolisib triplet in each study demonstrated the longest median duration of response results ever reported for a therapeutic regimen used in the primary analysis for a Phase 3 trial in the second-line HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer setting.”

VIKTORIA-1 PIK3CA Wild-Type Cohort Comparative Analysis

Dr. Sara Tolaney, Chief of the Division of Breast Oncology at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, presented a comparative analysis of data for the gedatolisib regimens from the PIK3CA wild-type cohort of VIKTORIA-1 and other regimens evaluated in patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer.

Eight studies were included in this network meta-analysis comparing progression-free survival outcomes in randomized controlled trials of systemic treatments evaluated among patients with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer with CDK4/6 inhibitor experience and PIK3CA wild-type tumors. This analysis found that the gedatolisib triplet and doublet each demonstrated statistically significant or numerically superior improvement in PFS and in progression-free survival rate at 6 months relative to the non-gedatolisib regimens evaluated. Of note, the analysis found that patients treated with the gedatolisib triplet and doublet were a statistically significant 2x and 1.5x more likely to survive without disease progression or death compared to imlunestrant plus abemaciclib, respectively.

About HR+/HER2- Breast Cancer

Breast cancer is the second most common cancer and one of the leading causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide.1 More than two million breast cancer cases were diagnosed globally in 2022.1 While survival rates are high for those diagnosed with early breast cancer, only approximately 30% of patients who are diagnosed with or who progress to metastatic disease are expected to live five years after their diagnosis.2 HR+/HER2- breast cancer is the most common subtype of breast cancer, accounting for approximately 70% of all breast cancers.2

About Celcuity

Celcuity is a biotechnology company focused on developing and commercializing targeted therapies for the treatment of multiple solid tumor indications. The company's first FDA-approved product is REVTORPYK™ (gedatolisib), pan-PI3K and mTORC1/2 inhibitor that comprehensively blockades the PAM (PI3K/AKT/mTOR) pathway. Its mechanism of action and pharmacokinetic properties are differentiated from other currently approved and investigational therapies that target PI3Kα, AKT or mTORC1 alone or together. A Phase 3 clinical trial, VIKTORIA-1, evaluating gedatolisib in combination with fulvestrant with or without palbociclib in patients with HR+/HER2- locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, supported FDA approval of REVTORPYK for use in patients without a PIK3CA mutation detected following progression on or after treatment with at least one line of endocrine therapy in the metastatic setting. Results for the PIK3CA mutant cohort of VIKTORIA-1 have been released. VIKTORIA-2 is an ongoing Phase 3 clinical trial incorporating two independent studies, Study 1 and Study 2, in two separate cohorts of patients with ABC who are treatment-naive in the advanced setting. Study 1 is evaluating gedatolisib plus palbociclib plus fulvestrant as first-line treatment for patients with endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- ABC. Study 2 is evaluating gedatolisib plus palbociclib plus letrozole as first-line treatment for patients with endocrine-sensitive HR+/HER2- ABC. A Phase 1/2 clinical trial, CELC-G-201, evaluating gedatolisib in combination with darolutamide in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, is ongoing. data.title: Bitdeer Reports 1,355 Bitcoin Mined In September While Building AI Capacity
data.description:
TL;DR: Bitdeer says its September Bitcoin production reached 1,355 BTC, highlighting the miner’s expanding hash rate alongside separate data-center and AI-service plans.

Bitdeer has released another sizable set of Bitcoin mining numbers as the industry weighs how much computing infrastructure should remain dedicated to hashing and how much can be redirected toward artificial intelligence services.

In its latest monthly operating update, published October 19, the company reported mining 1,355 BTC in September. It put the comparable figure a year earlier at 452 BTC, making the latest result roughly three times that level. The performance illustrates the consequences of adding mining capacity, though it does not by itself establish whether returns improved after power and equipment costs.

Hash rate is not profit

The company's report provides figures for its different computing operations, including a self-mining hash rate of 82.3 EH/s and co-mining capacity of 28.7 EH/s. Those categories refer to different arrangements and should not be combined carelessly into a single profit forecast.

A miner's monthly Bitcoin production reflects not only its hardware but also global network conditions. Difficulty adjustments, transaction fees, power availability and equipment efficiency change the number of coins that a given fleet can earn.

Even rising production can be accompanied by financial pressure if more competitors install machines or if the average cost of electricity rises. Investors should pair BTC output data with capital expenditure, cash costs and reported profitability before treating mined coins as free cash flow.

The separate opportunity in AI data centers

Bitdeer also describes an expanding pipeline for AI cloud and infrastructure services. The update references capacity agreements in Malaysia, with planned delivery windows extending into 2027 and 2028.

Those projects operate on a different commercial clock from a new Bitcoin miner brought online this month. A data-center agreement can represent future contracted capacity without proving that the site is finished, fully occupied or generating its forecast revenue today.

The convergence narrative has become popular among large miners because both industries need electricity, facilities and cooling. But the workloads use different processing hardware, and converting a mining site into AI infrastructure can require substantial additional investment.

Bitdeer's production update offers a useful snapshot of a company pursuing both routes. The near-term Bitcoin figures are realized operational results; the AI figures include plans and contracted capacity dependent on delivery.

That distinction will matter as analysts assess whether the company can sustain cash-generating mining operations while funding what may become a much larger infrastructure business over time.

data.title: BeOne Presents Compelling Data in Hard-to-Treat Liver and Lung Cancers at ESMO 2026
data.description:
BeOne Medicines Ltd. (; HKEX: 06160; ), a global oncology company, today announced new data from multiple differentiated investigational medicines across its priority solid tumor disease areas at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 (October 23–27, Madrid). The presentations span gastrointestinal, lung, and breast cancers, and reflect the growing momentum of BeOne’s solid tumor franchise.

Mark Lanasa, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer, Solid Tumors at BeOne, said:

“At ESMO, we are showing how our strategy of matching the right modality to disease biology is translating into meaningful clinical progress. Our GPC3 x 4-1BB bispecific antibody continues to be well tolerated and demonstrates durable activity with longer follow up in patients with heavily pre-treated hepatocellular carcinoma, while the first clinical data from our brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor and CEA-targeting ADC expand our innovation in non-small cell lung cancer. Alongside the global Phase 3 KANDELA-302 study of our CDK4 inhibitor in breast cancer, these advances mark a clear step forward as BeOne’s solid tumor pipeline moves from promising science toward medicines with the potential to improve outcomes in difficult-to-treat cancers.”

Potential first-in-class GPC3×4-1BB bispecific continues to demonstrate compelling and durable activity in heavily pretreated HCC (Proffered Paper: 1679O; October 24, 10:15–11:45 CET)

Patients with advanced HCC who progress after immunotherapy face a high unmet need, with no established standard of care and five-year survival of only approximately 20%1,2. BGB-B2033 is an investigational bispecific antibody designed to address this gap by activating 4-1BB on T cells in the presence of GPC3-expressing tumor cells, concentrating immune activation at the tumor site, and limiting systemic toxicity, a key consideration for HCC patients who frequently suffer from underlying liver disease.

Updated Phase 1 results include the first disclosure of dose-optimization data and longer follow-up from dose escalation. Among 94 patients, 93.6% had received prior PD-(L)1 therapy and 61.7% had received both PD-(L)1 therapy and a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Highlights include:

  • At the recommended Phase 3 dose of 450 mg every three weeks, the confirmed objective response rate (ORR) was 36.0%, a result that exceeds efficacy observed with TKIs, which have shown an ORR of approximately 5% in late-line HCC.3

  • At the selected Phase 3 dose, the estimated six-month confirmed duration-of-response rate was 74.1%, with responses observed across all clinically relevant patient subgroups.

  • Across dose levels, Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 5.3% of patients, and treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation in only 2.1%.

BGB-B2033 received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in December 2025, as well as Orphan Drug Designation from the FDA in March 2026 and the European Commission in October 2026 for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). BeOne plans to initiate global registrational clinical trials in late-line HCC by the end of 2026, while also developing plans for registrational studies in earlier treatment settings.

Initial first-in-human data from two differentiated assets advance BeOne’s emerging NSCLC portfolio

At ESMO 2026, BeOne is presenting initial clinical data in NSCLC from two biomarker-led programs with distinct mechanisms: the oral, brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor, BGB-58067, and the CEA-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC), BG-C477. Based on these promising data, both programs are intended to advance toward late-stage development in 2027, continuing to build BeOne’s footprint in lung cancer alongside its established program with TEVIMBRA (tislelizumab).

Brain-penetrant PRMT5 inhibitor, BGB-58067, demonstrates systemic and intracranial activity in MTAP-deficient NSCLC (Poster: 1043P; October 23, 3:15–4:00 PM CET)

BGB-58067 is a highly potent, brain-penetrant methylthioadenosine (MTA)-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitor designed to exploit the vulnerability created by MTAP deficiency. In this, the largest publicly shared data set in MTAP-deficient solid tumors, initial Phase 1 findings from 182 patients, including 83 with NSCLC, showed:

  • Among 75 efficacy-evaluable patients with MTAP-deficient NSCLC, confirmed ORR was 25.3% and disease control rate (DCR) was 76.0%. In the EGFR wild-type subgroup, confirmed ORR was 38.5% and DCR was 82.1%.

  • Median progression-free survival was 7.7 months in the overall NSCLC cohort and 8.1 months in the EGFR wild-type subgroup.

  • In the NSCLC cohort, an intracranial objective response rate of 30.8% was observed in patients with untreated, asymptomatic brain metastases as well as a low rate of central nervous system (CNS) progression in 2L+ NSCLC.

  • At daily doses of 200–400 mg (n=87), Grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events occurred in 27.6%, and treatment-related adverse events led to discontinuation in 5.7%. The most common treatment-related events were nausea, anemia and fatigue.

CEA-targeting ADC BG-C477 achieves encouraging response rate in previously-treated CEAhigh NSCLC (Poster: 2567P; October 26, 12:00–12:45 PM CET)

BG-C477 is the first ADC to emerge from BeOne’s internal drug discovery organization. With a proprietary CEA (or CEACAM5) targeting antibody, a highly stable conjugator, and a cleavable linker, BG-C477 is designed to deliver a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor payload directly to CEA-expressing tumor cells.

As of April 9, 2026, preliminary Phase 1 monotherapy findings from 43 heavily pretreated patients with NSCLC, including 25 with high CEA expression, showed:

  • Confirmed ORR was 56.0% in patients with CEAhigh NSCLC, with a disease control rate of 88.0%; confirmed ORR in the overall NSCLC population was 34.9%.

  • Among patients with CEAhigh NSCLC, median duration of response had not been reached. The majority of responders, as well as two patients with unconfirmed responses, remained on treatment at data cutoff.

  • Grade 3 or higher treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were predominantly hematologic events (anemia 14.0%, neutropenia 14.0%, thrombocytopenia 2.3%).

Updated results, with a more recent data cut-off, will be presented in the Locally Advanced NSCLC poster session on Monday, October 26 at 12:00 CET. BG-C477 received Fast Track Designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in October 2026.

Pivotal-study update: Phase 3 KANDELA-302 trial of CDK4 inhibitor BGB-43395 now enrolling in first-line HR+/HER2-negative breast cancer (1885TiP; October 24, 12:00–12:45 PM CEST)

Building on previously reported Phase 1 activity and tolerability findings, BeOne is advancing BGB-43395, an investigational selective CDK4 inhibitor, in the global Phase 3 KANDELA-302 study (NCT07492641). The study compares BGB-43395 plus letrozole with investigator’s choice of abemaciclib, palbociclib or ribociclib plus letrozole in first-line HR+/HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

Enrollment began in May 2026, with patients planned across North and South America, Europe, Asia and Australia. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, with overall survival as the key secondary endpoint.

About BGB-B2033

BGB-58067 is an investigational, oral small molecule designed to inhibit protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) in an MTA-dependent manner, enabling selective targeting of MTAP-deleted cancer cells. data.title: Demeter's Ashwini Agarwal sees value in largecaps, financial services and consumer stocks; avoids IT and OMCs
data.description:
Ashwini Agarwal, Founder and Partner at Demeter Advisors, believes large-cap stocks offer better return potential than midcaps and smallcaps over the next 12 months, following the recent correction in Indian equity markets.

He sees opportunities in financial services, consumer staples, pharmaceuticals, chemicals and select manufacturing companies, where stock prices have fallen despite businesses continuing to perform.

The recent sell-off has widened the valuation gap between largecap and smallcap stocks, making the former more attractive relative to their earnings growth, Agarwal said.

He added, “On a bottom-up basis, there are still opportunities in the wider market. But on a top-down basis, the chances that you make money on largecaps over the next 12 months are far higher than you will make money in smallcaps at an index level that's how I think about it. So opportunities exist, but on a top-down basis, largecaps look far more attractive.”

According to Agarwal, the Nifty has delivered annualised returns of around 5% since December 2022, while earnings have grown by about 8% annually. In contrast, the Nifty 250 smallcap index has risen by around 9% annually, against earnings growth of approximately 6%. This suggests that largecap valuations have declined while smallcap valuations have expanded over the same period.

Agarwal believes the correction has created opportunities for long-term investors, particularly in stocks where earnings have improved but valuations have fallen.

However, he cautioned that uncertainty around global energy and transportation costs, along with fluctuations in raw material prices, could affect corporate earnings.

"Staples are giving an entry opportunity," Agarwal said, pointing to opportunities in consumer staples and tobacco stocks. He believes some of these companies have seen significant corrections, even as their businesses continue to offer value. Strong dividend yields could also provide support to investors in select stocks.

Financial services is another area he favours. Agarwal said earnings in the sector have improved over the past six months, but share prices have not reflected the improvement. Credit quality remains healthy, spreads are stable and liquidity conditions, although tighter recently, remain manageable.

Within financial services, he favours select private-sector banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs). He also sees potential in microfinance stocks, where valuations have fallen substantially over the past three to four years. Some companies are trading below their book value, although he acknowledged that drought-related stress could affect parts of the sector.

He also sees opportunities in offline retail, particularly clothing, where valuations have fallen sharply. While the shift towards online shopping has affected the sector, he believes the decline in stock prices has been more severe than the underlying business performance warrants.

Select chemical and pharmaceutical companies have also become attractive following recent corrections. Agarwal believes investors should take a longer-term view of these sectors rather than focus only on near-term concerns around input costs and earnings.

Agarwal remains positive on Indian exporters, including apparel and engineering companies, as well as businesses in chemicals and contract development and manufacturing. He believes expanding export markets and the ability of Indian companies to meet specialised customer requirements could support growth over the next three years.

He is also comfortable holding hospital stocks despite concerns around regulatory intervention and possible price caps. Agarwal argued that hospitals need sustainable returns to attract investment and expand capacity, particularly given India's shortage of hospital infrastructure.

On information technology services, however, he remains cautious. He said the impact of artificial intelligence on the sector's business model is still unclear, making it difficult to assess the industry's long-term earnings outlook.

Agarwal added policy uncertainty remains a key concern for investors in oil marketing companies (OMCs) and gas companies. He noted that oil companies do not have complete freedom to set petrol and diesel prices, which creates uncertainty around their earnings despite fluctuations in crude oil prices.

Agarwal said frequent policy changes across sectors, including hospitals, insurance distribution and brokerage services, have made investors cautious. He stressed the need for a stable policy framework over the next five years, adding that sudden regulatory changes could affect companies' earnings and investment decisions.

data.title: Reliance Jio Platforms IPO GMP, allotment date, listing date, time, overall subscription status; QIB, NII, Retail, RIL
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Reliance Jio Platforms' Rs.30,213-crore initial public offering has concluded its subscription process, setting the stage for the allotment announcement on October 26, 2026. Investors who applied for shares will be able to verify their allotment through the official websites of BSE, NSE and KFin Technologies, the registrar to the issue.

The IPO, backed by Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries Limited (RIL), attracted substantial investor interest during its three-day bidding window. Meanwhile, the reported grey market premium (GMP) of Rs.250 has indicated a potential listing price above the issue's upper price band.

While the allotment is expected to be finalised on October 26, shares will be credited to investors' demat account on October 27. Meanwhile, refunds for those investors who didn't get allotment will also be processed the same day.

The company is scheduled to list on the stock exchanges BSE and NSE on October 28 at 10 am.

The allotment is expected to be finalised on October 26, according to the tentative timetable. Investors can use any of the following platforms to check their application status once the results are available.

Investors can follow these steps to check their application details through the National Stock Exchange:

Visit the NSE IPO bid verification page: https://www.nseindia.com/invest/check-trades-bids-verify-ipo-bids

Select 'Equity & SME IPO bid details'.

Open the 'Select Symbol' dropdown menu and choose 'JPL'.

Enter your PAN details or application number.

Click 'Submit' to view the application details.

Applicants can also use the Bombay Stock Exchange's online application-status facility:

Visit the BSE IPO application status page: https://www.bseindia.com/investors/appli_check

Select the relevant IPO from the list, if it is available.

Choose the permitted identification option.

Enter the required details.

Submit the request to check the application status.

KFin Technologies is the registrar to the Jio Platforms IPO. Applicants can use the registrar's website to check their allotment:

Visit the official website: https://ipostatus.kfintech.com/

Under 'Select IPO', choose 'Jio Platforms Ltd'.

Enter your IPO application number, PAN or Demat account number.

Click 'Submit' to view the allotment status.

The IPO closed on Friday after receiving bids for 421.87 crore shares against 19.75 crore shares on offer. The overall issue was subscribed 22.19 times by the end of the three-day bidding period.

Institutional investors accounted for the strongest demand. The qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion was subscribed 70.55 times, while the non-institutional investors (NII) category received bids equivalent to 14 times the shares reserved for it.

The retail investor segment was subscribed 2.72 times. Meanwhile, the employee reservation portion recorded 2.93 times subscription, and the shareholder reservation category was subscribed 7.60 times.

The Jio Platforms IPO's grey market premium stood at Rs.250, according to media reports. Based on the upper end of the issue price band at Rs.1,119 per share, this translated into an indicative listing price of Rs.1,369.

The implied premium represented a potential gain of approximately 22.34% over the upper issue price.

However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of investor sentiment, not a confirmed listing price. It can change before the shares begin trading, and the actual listing price will depend on market demand and trading conditions on the debut date.

Jio Platforms, the digital and telecommunications subsidiary of Reliance Industries, launched its public issue to raise Rs.30,213 crore. The IPO comprised a fresh issue of 27 crore shares and did not include an offer-for-sale (OFS) component.

According to the company's red herring prospectus (RHP), Rs.27,500 crore from the proceeds will be used to repay borrowings of its wholly owned telecom subsidiary, Reliance Jio Infocomm Ltd (RJIL). The remaining proceeds will be allocated towards general corporate purposes.

The issue price band was set at Rs.1,065-1,119 per share, and one lot comprised 12 shares. The IPO also reserved up to 46,94,836 shares for employees, offered at a discount of Rs.54 per share to the issue price.

Jio Platforms raised Rs.8,109.85 crore from anchor investors, with the anchor bidding date scheduled for October 19, 2026.

The company operates a technology platform that combines digital connectivity with consumer and enterprise services. Its portfolio includes mobile networks, fixed broadband, cloud capabilities, applications and proprietary technology.

Kotak Mahindra Capital Company Ltd and Morgan Stanley India Company Pvt Ltd are the book-running lead managers for the IPO, while KFin Technologies Ltd is the registrar. The shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on October 28, 2026.
